governance.note: Inherits every measured lever of the neiso-28 hydro-codramp keeper UNCHANGED (the daily Algonquin Citygate gas-basis from real EIA Natural Gas Weekly Update spot prints + Transco Z6 NY daily-basis shape; historic CAMPD unit-level outage windows; EIA-860 cogen BTM CHP host-steam pulled out of the LP; measured F923 per-plant monthly delivered gas under the measured monthly AGT hub-basis overlay; measured EIA-930 net interchange; measured EIA-860 dual-fuel switching at the delivered oil price; the 2025 hydro repin to the measured EIA-930 NG:WAT monthly grid total with 2024-vintage backfill; the storage vintage ramp; and the COD/retirement off-ramps for all resource classes) and adds ONE structural fix plus ONE reporting fix, both measured-data corrections that regenerate for a forward year and respond to changed conditions: (1) BIOMASS MEASURED MUST-RUN INJECTION -- biomass is now injected for NEISO (and every non-ERCOT per-plant ISO) as a fixed must-run profile from its measured EIA-923 annual+monthly energy, exactly like ERCOT, and the raw biomass LP units are dropped from the per-plant fleet so it is not served twice. This fixes a STRUCTURAL inconsistency: the non-ERCOT path had kept biomass as a dispatchable LP unit burning at a flat low delivered MC with no annual-energy cap, so when 2025 gas rose ($2.19->$3.52 HH + winter AGT basis) the LP ran biomass deep in-merit to ~5.28 TWh vs the measured ~2.45. Real NEISO biomass is fuel-supply/contract limited (~2.45-3.0 TWh) and roughly price-insensitive; the injection pins it to measured energy and makes it price-insensitive, which is physically correct. The injected energy uses the SAME vintage-carry reconciliation the benchmark uses (prior complete year x EIA-930 vintage completeness for the partial 2025 survey), so injected biomass == benchmark biomass by construction -- it is a measured physical input, NOT a pin to model output and NOT tuned to any residual. (2) LIKE-FOR-LIKE TOTAL + ENERGY-BALANCE GUARD -- the report's [1] generation TOTAL is now anchored to the EIA-930 measured grid total (net generation = demand + net interchange) every year: itemized EIA-930 fuels + EIA-930-repaired renewables + carried biomass + an explicit unspecified 'other' residual (net_gen - the itemized sum), with the model's injected OTHER class shown as its own row. A per-year energy-balance diagnostic asserts model generation lands on the measured net generation. This removes a BENCHMARK-ASSEMBLY artifact (EIA-930's itemized series omit biomass and an 'other' residual, so a raw itemized TOTAL undercounts true in-region generation) that had made model-minus-actual TOTAL swing +4/+5/-4 across 2023/24/25; it is now a consistent +0.10/+0.13/+0.23 TWh. This is a reporting/benchmark-reconciliation change, not a dispatch change. No adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to a price or volume residual; no unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled so model output lands on actuals. The gas-offer / daily-AGT path is untouched, so the winter scarcity mechanism (gas->oil switching) is preserved.
governance.validation_note: Biomass fix lands exactly as designed: 2025 model biomass 2.45 TWh vs measured 2.45 (was 5.28), 2024 2.96, 2023 3.00 -- now price-insensitive and matched to EIA-923 every year. Energy balance is clean and consistent: model gen - EIA-930 net gen = +0.10 / +0.13 / +0.23 TWh (2023/24/25), and the headline TOTAL gap no longer flips sign. The hydro/COD/storage/AGT levers do NOT regress: 2025 hydro 5.11 vs EIA-930 5.12 (preserved); oil burn 1.50 vs 1.24 (near actual, vs neiso-28 1.39); price max 271.85 $/MWh (vs 258.98); storage discharge IMPROVES to -52.0% (0.998 vs 2.08 TWh; PS discharge 0.76 vs neiso-28 0.54). 2023/2024 do NOT swing materially (2023 gas 54.24 / mean LMP 33.96; 2024 gas 58.84 / mean LMP 39.35 -- gas moves <0.7 TWh, mean LMP <0.4 vs neiso-28). The COST of the fix, fully expected per CLAUDE.md #1/#11: removing the ~2.8 TWh of phantom 2025 biomass surfaces a measured-data categorization gap -- the model serves the freed load with gas (the marginal fuel), but EIA-930 attributes ~1.8 TWh of it to UNSPECIFIED 'other' (EIA-930 2025 other residual 4.40 TWh vs the model's measured EIA-923 OTHER injection 2.61). So 2025 gas overshoots to 61.87 vs actual 60.09 (+3.0%), CC_REGULAR to +3.64 TWh (+1.4pp), and the 2025 mean LMP to +12.8% (cheap in-merit biomass no longer suppresses the marginal price -- physically correct, since real biomass is must-run and price-taking). These are MODEL MISSes whose root cause is the OTHER/residual data gap, NOT closable by tuning gas offers (explicitly out of scope, CLAUDE.md #1/#11). neiso-29 is the keeper because it is the most structurally faithful run -- biomass behaves like the fuel/contract-limited resource it is instead of swinging ~2x with gas -- not because it has the lowest gate error (it is worse on C1/C2/C3a than neiso-28, which reached those numbers partly through the biomass-on-margin artifact this run removes).

exceptions.reason: Grew from neiso-28's +1.05 TWh as a DIRECT, expected consequence of the correct biomass must-run fix (CLAUDE.md #1/#11: a structurally-correct measured input stays in even when it worsens a residual). Removing the ~2.8 TWh of phantom 2025 biomass frees load that the LP now serves with gas (the marginal fuel). neiso-28's lower CC residual was reached partly through the biomass-on-margin artifact this run removes. The deeper root cause is a measured-data categorization gap: EIA-930 puts ~1.8 TWh of 2025 NEISO generation in an unspecified 'other' residual (EIA-930 other 4.40 TWh vs the model's measured EIA-923 OTHER injection 2.61), so gas absorbs what EIA-930 calls 'other'. This is an EIA-923-OTHER-vs-EIA-930-residual reconciliation item for a follow-up, explicitly NOT to be closed by tuning a gas offer curve to the residual.

Same root cause as C1: with biomass correctly pinned to 2.45 TWh, the freed 2025 load is served by gas, which overshoots actual by 1.78 TWh because EIA-930 attributes ~1.8 TWh of in-region generation to an unspecified 'other' residual the model's measured EIA-923 OTHER injection (2.61) does not reach. Total model generation matches the measured grid total (model gen 107.39 vs EIA-930 net gen 107.15, +0.23 TWh), so this is an intra-mix gas-vs-other allocation gap, not over-generation. A measured-data reconciliation follow-up; not closable by a gas-offer tune (CLAUDE.md #1/#11).

Rose from neiso-28's +3.2% as a consequence of the correct biomass must-run mechanism: biomass is now netted from demand and never sets price (it is must-run and price-taking in reality), so in hours where the over-dispatched cheap biomass had been on the margin the price is now set by gas. The mechanism is more faithful; the residual LEVEL over-prediction is the same gas-offer-level calibration item that drives C1/C2, plus the OTHER/residual gas overshoot. Out of scope here and explicitly NOT to be closed by re-tuning the gas input to the price residual (CLAUDE.md #1/#11).

Unchanged from neiso-28 and out of scope for this run. Every gas tranche flagged dual-fuel by EIA-860 is capped at the delivered oil price (~$18/MMBtu), so the cleared LMP tops out near the oil-peaker cost (model 2025 max 271.85) and never exceeds $300. The real >$300 scarcity hours come from single-fuel gas bidding the full AGT spot (~$27-36/MMBtu on the coldest days) and from ORDC/reserve scarcity pricing, neither fully represented. An open structural item for a follow-up (single-fuel gas offer at AGT spot; reserve scarcity), NOT addressed by the biomass/total fixes and NOT to be closed by tuning the gas input to the residual.

The remaining gap is under-modeled PS arbitrage / multi-day cycling and reserve value -- a separate follow-up item unchanged in scope here, NOT closable by re-pinning storage to its observed throughput.
